beginner.summary: For Python developers, data engineers and ML engineers who have used embeddings or a relational database but have not run a vector database. Covers running Qdrant in Docker with the Web UI, the collection, point, vector and payload data model, distance metrics, the Python qdrant-client in server and local mode, embedding text with FastEmbed, upserts, bulk loading, nearest-neighbour queries with query_points, payload filters and payload indexes, scroll and count, payload updates, named vectors, recommendation and grouping queries, collection aliases, snapshots, and a semantic document search capstone.
prerequisites: Writes Python 3 scripts with functions, virtual environments and pip installs
Runs Docker containers and uses curl or an HTTP client to call a JSON REST API
Understands at a high level what an embedding vector is and why similar texts get similar vectors
outcomes: Run Qdrant locally with persistent storage and manage collections through the REST API, Web UI and Python client
Embed text with FastEmbed, load points in bulk and answer nearest-neighbour queries with query_points
Combine vector search with payload filters backed by the right payload indexes, and page through data with scroll and count
Protect a collection with aliases and snapshots and ship a filtered semantic document search with measured hit rate

intermediate.summary: For engineers who already run single-node Qdrant search with filters and want production-grade retrieval quality and efficiency. Covers sparse vectors with the IDF modifier, BM25 and SPLADE through FastEmbed, multi-stage Query API pipelines with prefetch, hybrid search with RRF and DBSF fusion, ColBERT multivectors, Matryoshka coarse-to-fine retrieval, discovery and context queries, order_by and sampling, formula-based score boosting, facets and the distance matrix, HNSW tuning and filtered search behaviour, segments and optimizers, storage modes, scalar, binary and product quantization, nested filters, payload-based multitenancy, the Helm chart on Kubernetes, and a hybrid search capstone.
prerequisites: Has built a Qdrant collection with payload indexes and filtered query_points calls, or completed the Qdrant beginner level
Can compute retrieval metrics such as recall@k and MRR from labelled queries in Python
Has Docker and kubectl access to a local Kubernetes such as kind or minikube
outcomes: Build dense, sparse, multivector and fused hybrid retrieval pipelines with the Query API
Tune HNSW, optimizer and storage settings and prove the effect with recall and latency measurements
Cut memory with scalar, binary or product quantization while holding recall with rescoring and oversampling
Serve many tenants from one collection and run Qdrant on Kubernetes with the official Helm chart

advanced.summary: For platform engineers, SREs and architects who operate Qdrant for production workloads. Covers distributed mode with Raft consensus, shard and replica planning, write and read consistency, shard transfers, user-defined sharding with shard keys, changing shard counts, failure recovery, shard snapshots and S3 storage for disaster recovery, API keys, JWT role-based access control, TLS and mutual TLS, strict mode, Prometheus metrics and alerting, slow-query diagnosis, bulk ingestion tuning including GPU indexing, capacity planning, rolling upgrades and migrations, Qdrant Cloud managed as code, Hybrid Cloud on your own Kubernetes, and a production multi-tenant cluster capstone.
prerequisites: Has tuned HNSW, quantization and payload indexes on Qdrant, or completed the Qdrant intermediate level
Operates Docker Compose and Kubernetes workloads, including StatefulSets, Secrets and Helm releases
Reads Prometheus metrics and writes basic Grafana dashboards and alert rules
outcomes: Build and operate a multi-node Qdrant cluster with planned sharding, replication and consistency settings
Recover from node loss and disasters using replica transfers, shard snapshots and tested runbooks
Secure Qdrant with API keys, JWT RBAC, TLS and strict mode, and monitor it with Prometheus and Grafana
Size, tune, upgrade and run Qdrant on Qdrant Cloud, Hybrid Cloud or self-managed Kubernetes
